subject: Post-call: hosted API pricing — quick numbers we need
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@lumensys.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hosted API pricing — quick numbers we need

Thanks again for taking time earlier, Claire — good conversation and I think there’s a clear path to get you comfortable with hosted pricing. Quick recap + the minimum items we need to move to a firm quote: 

Recap (2-min):
- You want hosted API (no private infra to start) for a customer-facing assistant + a small batch embeddings job for search.
- Key concern is predictable unit economics during peak shopping windows (10–15 minute spikes).
- SOC2 + basic IP protections required; procurement will want an initial SOW.

Can you confirm the following estimates so we can lock a pricing band: 
1) Expected monthly token volume (give range if unsure) — include both prompts and generated tokens; if you track completed tokens separately, please add both.
2) Typical composition: what percent of calls are generation (free-form completion) vs short structured responses vs embeddings jobs?
3) Peak throughput — your 99th-percentile concurrent requests or requests/sec over a 5–10 minute window. If you have an observed highest 10-minute window, that number is ideal.
4) Target budget — ballpark $/1M tokens you’re trying to hit for hosted (if you have a preferred committed vs pay-as-you-go model please call it out).
5) Timing / contract horizon you’d like for any commit (monthly, 12-month).

I attached a blank template (lumensys_traffic_estimate.xlsx) — if it’s easier, drop numbers directly into the sheet and reply. Once we have these we’ll: (a) validate model selection and caching/embedding strategies with our Solutions Engineer, (b) provide two hosted options — a small commit band and a pay-as-you-go baseline — and (c) surface any latency SLO expectations that would affect pricing.

Next step: if it’s okay I’ll loop Marissa (Solutions Eng) for a 30-min technical sync to validate the traffic shape and KV/prefix caching opportunities.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: lumensys_traffic_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Claire Dunn <claire@lumensys.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 19:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted API pricing — quick numbers we need

Hi Rishi — thanks, that template is helpful. Quick answers below and I attached a production traffic snapshot as well.

1) Monthly tokens: our initial expectation is 5M–8M tokens/month during the pilot (we expect growth after Q4). We can commit to 6M/mo for the pilot if pricing is within range.
2) Composition: ~70% generation (assistant responses), ~20% prompts/short structured answers, ~10% embeddings (the embeddings jobs are batch-offline but show up as spikes when we reindex). Note: average generation length is ~150 tokens per completion, prompts ~40 tokens.
3) Peak: our engineers sampled prod and saw short windows where request rate for the assistant hit ~220 requests/sec (spiky behavior for ~8–12 minutes during promotions). Ability to burst is important.
4) Target budget: we’re aiming for ~$40–$55 per 1M tokens for hosted API given we want to avoid early heavy operational lift. If commit is required, 6M/mo at $45/1M would be attractive.
5) Contract horizon: for now pilot is 3 months with option to convert to 12-month commit after validation.

Attached: lumensys_prod_pattern.png (screenshot of a 24h spike window).

Happy to jump on the technical sync — Marissa’s name is familiar, she can be on the call.

—Claire
Director, Product
Lumen Systems

Attachments: lumensys_prod_pattern.png (png)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@lumensys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted API pricing — quick numbers we need

Claire — this is great, thanks for the clear numbers. A few clarifications and what we can do next: 

Clarifications:
- Your 220 req/sec peak is really the driver here. We typically look at token throughput as the pricing risk surface, but request spikes of that shape (8–12m) materially increase cost unless prefix/KV caching and batching reduce effective tokens served.
- Embeddings: even though they’re 10% of calls, they may be small in token volume, but batch reindex windows can create short heavy token bursts — worth engineering attention.

High-level options we can put on paper quickly:
A) Pay-as-you-go hosted: list baseline ~$70 per 1M tokens (no commit). Good if you want zero commitment and full elastic capacity.
B) Small commit pilot: 6M/mo committed -> target $50/1M tokens; with a 3:1 burst allowance (you can exceed committed rate for short windows up to 3x without reprice inside the monthly bucket).
C) Pilot special: 6M/mo at $45/1M with a short SOW + 3-month pilot term (requires sign-off from pricing ops; we’ll need procurement contact copied and a quick SOW).

Which of those is closest to what you had in mind? If C looks good we’ll: (1) draft a short SOW and pricing term sheet, (2) schedule a 30-minute technical call with Marissa to walk traffic snapshots and caching/quantization opportunities, and (3) validate SLOs (99th latency targets) so we can confirm the burst policy.

I attached a quick snapshot of our current hosted pricing (redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf) to set expectations. Jordan — can you prepare a short runbook for Marissa ahead of the tech sync (KV/cache flags, sample payload sizes, any auth throttles)?

Thanks — I’ll wait on your preference and will start the paperwork if you want option C.

Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted API pricing — quick numbers we need

Looping in a short internal checklist before we run the tech sync with Lumen Systems: 
- I’ll ask for a small sample of real payloads (anonymized) + the lumensys_prod_pattern.png Claire sent.
- Verify average tokens per completion (they said ~150) and measure median vs 99th token lengths.
- Prepare a caching note: if 40% of prompts are repeated or templated, we can likely reduce billed tokens significantly via prefix caching.
- Prepare an ops note on burst handling: for a 3:1 burst policy we need to validate their worst-case concurrency and whether any single customer will fan out requests.

I’ll be available Monday 10–12 PT for the customer call. Rishi — can you confirm the calendar invite and copy procurement if they want the SOW draft up front?

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
